summary: The Domain trust page passes the browser review at 1280 px and 390 px. All 112 cells show the preview verdict as a word. The failure-mode list has 61 entries, one for each non-safe cell. The score table equals the base export. No page shows a wrong or stale result. Eleven nonblocking findings remain.

accessibility_snapshots: Aria snapshot of #trust-table at 1280 px: 9 columnheader (Model, A to H), 14 rowheader, 112 cell in the preview order (51 safe, 14 'Safe, not optimized', 33 risk, 14 unproven), and one region named 'Domain trust matrix'. Excerpt: row "Claude Haiku 5.5 2 OpenCode · 0 Pi · 2 runs safe safe safe Safe, not optimized safe safe safe safe".
Aria snapshot of #trust-table at 390 px: the same tree and the same 112 cell words in the same order.

Axe-core on #domain-trust: 23 rules pass at 1280 px and 24 at 390 px. One violation at each width, link-in-text-block (UX-P3-2). Color-contrast is incomplete because of translucent backgrounds, so manual contrast values cover the cells and the text.
interactions: Keyboard: Tab from the page top reached the link 'How the verdict rule works' and then the region 'Domain trust matrix' (27 presses at 1280 px, 28 at 390 px). The focus ring is 2 px solid rgb(226, 178, 90). At 390 px four ArrowRight presses scrolled the matrix 160 px.
Click on 'How the verdict rule works' opened methodology.html#domain-trust at 1280 px and 390 px. The heading sits under the sticky navigation bar (UX-P3-3).
Matrix scrolled to the right end at 390 px: columns E to H show and the Model column leaves the view (ux-p3-r2-390-scrolled.png).
Request interception tests: a 2.5 s data delay, a blocked data request, data without domain_trust, an empty models list, a malformed block, HTML in string fields, and markup in numeric fields.
Viewport checks at 1280x900, 390x844 (touch emulation, device scale 2), and 320x640 (no sideways page scroll).

nonblocking_findings: UX-P3-1 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The domain column headers show only the letters A to H. No title, tooltip, or legend names a domain. The heatmap above shows titles as tooltips, and data.domains holds them. A lead cannot link a column to a kind of work. Rationale: the track answers which model fits which kind of work.

UX-P3-2 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The link 'How the verdict rule works' has no underline. Its color contrast with the paragraph text is 1.2 to 1. Axe reports link-in-text-block (serious, WCAG 1.4.1) at both widths. The global rule a { text-decoration: none } in docs/assets/css/site.css causes this. Rationale: a reader who cannot see the hue can miss the only link of the rule paragraph.

UX-P3-3 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The link to methodology.html#domain-trust lands with the section heading under the sticky navigation bar. The bar is 66 px high at 1280 px and 149 px high at 390 px. The heading starts 21 px from the top. site.css has no scroll-margin-top or scroll-padding-top, and the older anchor #sources behaves the same. Rationale: the new link shows an existing site-wide gap.

UX-P3-4 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The failure-mode list is a flat list with one long entry for each cell. The longest entry has 1,371 characters (MiMo V2.6 Flash, G). Each entry repeats the model name, so the list is not visibly grouped by model (spec design decision 6). A check prints twice when it failed and has coverage below N_MIN (Hy3 C P.n-plus-one, Hy3 D P.dedup-item). At 390 px the section is about 19,000 px high. Rationale: a lead cannot scan the list. Suggested fix: one heading for each model with a nested list.

UX-P3-5 [Nit] ux-browser-review: Some list wording is unclear. A check graded above the threshold reads 'graded 9 of 2 needed'. Five checks show registry split notes as their meaning: B.image-response, C.filter-case, D.history-status, F.auth-return, and F.lifecycle (for example 'spec: C.3 — split: ...'). The notes name internal criterion ids. They come from harness/tests/meta/spec-matrix-contract.ts:31-35, which the suite hash covers (NFR-2). Rationale: a public reader cannot decode them. Suggested fix: rewrite the display text in harness/domain_trust.py, not at the source.

UX-P3-6 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The scroll hint has no CSS on results.html. Only real-work.html and review.html style the class .scroll-hint, in an inline style block. On results.html it shows as a 16 px paragraph in the body color. It also shows at 1280 px, where the matrix fits (scroll width 1071 px, client width 1071 px). Rationale: the hint looks brighter than the lede and gives a false instruction on desktop.

UX-P3-7 [Nit] ux-browser-review: At 390 px the Model column is not sticky. After a reader scrolls the matrix to columns E to H, the model names leave the view (ux-p3-r2-390-scrolled.png). The heatmap above has the same pattern. Rationale: a reader cannot tell which model a verdict belongs to.

UX-P3-8 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The verdict unproven uses the class cell-dead, the 0% color of the heatmap. This color is a dull red-brown close to the risk color. The word separates the two verdicts, so NFR-6 holds. Rationale: the color suggests a near-failure, but unproven means no evidence. Suggested fix: a neutral grey.

UX-P3-9 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The Hy3 row reads '1 runs', because the count line always prints 'runs'. The methodology section explains N_MIN but does not state its value, 2. Only the failure-mode labels show 'of 2 needed'. Rationale: small copy gaps.

UX-P3-10 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The domain_trust code shares the try/catch of the whole results page. A block without a models list replaces the score table with 'Could not load benchmark data: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')'. An absent block leaves an empty Domain trust section with the scroll hint. An empty models list prints 'No failure modes.'. The exporter writes none of these shapes at this head. Rationale: resilience gap.

UX-P3-11 [Nit] ux-browser-review: The page inserts six numeric fields into HTML without escapeHtml: runs.opencode, runs.pi, runs.total, failed, graded, and rule.n_min. The code comment says the page escapes every value. A test with markup in these fields created six elements. The string fields (model name, check id, kind, text, verdict) pass the escape test. The exporter writes integers only. Rationale: hardening gap.
evidence: HEAD matched 6f7451be5013c7d4e6ffc30db92b0205984baaac at the start and at the end. The worktree shows only the untracked runs link, and git diff HEAD -- docs is empty.
The phase diff c4560f2..6f7451b changes docs/results.html, docs/methodology.html, README.md, docs/assets/data/*.json, and non-UX files. docs/assets/css and docs/assets/js do not change.

Setup: python3 -m http.server 8767 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs (PID 3655780), PROJECT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8767/results.html. The role stopped only that PID. Chrome 157.0.8103.78 ran headless through heavy-run.sh with Playwright. Viewports: 1280x900, 390x844 (touch, device scale 2), and 320x640.

Expectations come from measure/tracks/domain_trust/preview.json: 14 models, 58 unique runs, n_min 2, 112 cells (51 safe, 14 unoptimized, 33 risk, 14 unproven). That gives 61 non-safe cells. The number 63 in test-strategy.md section 8 step 6 is stale.
Step 1 pass at both widths: the h2 'Domain trust' follows the score table and the heatmap (page tops at 1280 px: score table 902, heatmap 3498, Domain trust 4299).
Step 2 pass: 14 rows in model-id order, header cells Model and A to H, 8 verdict cells in each row, and unique row names.
Step 3 pass: each of the 112 cells shows the preview verdict as a word at both widths. The word counts are 51 safe, 14 'Safe, not optimized', 33 risk, and 14 unproven.

Step 4 pass: nine sampled cells equal the preview and the brief. claude-haiku-5-5 D is 'Safe, not optimized'. hy3 F, mimo-v2.6-flash B, longcat-2.0 G, and muse-spark-1.3-contributor F are risk. gpt-5.6-luna B and hy3 C are unproven. muse-spark-1.3-contributor B and E are safe.

Step 4 list text: LongCat-2.0 G reads 'G.401 — spec: all methods require staff — graded 3 of 2 needed — failed 3', which is 3 failed of 3 graded. Hy3 C reads 'P.n-plus-one — performance: per-row query inside the list render — graded 1 of 2 needed — failed 1'. No entry holds 'not graded'.

Step 5 pass: each row reads 'N OpenCode · N Pi · N runs'. The numbers equal the export and an independent read of runs/<id>/artifacts/provenance.json for all 58 runs. The arm_a and arm_b counts equal the a- and b- run id prefixes.

Step 6 pass: 61 list entries, one for each non-safe cell, in model order then domain order. No safe cell has an entry. Each entry equals the text rebuilt from the export data, and the export data equals the preview in every failure count, graded count, and gap id. The page prints 251 coverage labels, equal to the count from the preview.

Step 7 pass: the rule paragraph says 'safe means no failure in the checks that ran, not proof that a defect is absent'. It links to ./methodology.html#domain-trust, and a click opens that anchor at both widths.

Methodology check pass at both widths: one section id="domain-trust" with no nested section, an ordered list of four verdicts (risk, unproven, unoptimized, safe), a 15-row probe table with three cells in each row, the words 'not graded', N_MIN, and the three kinds. No horizontal overflow at 390 px.

Step 8 pass: Chrome renders the same text for the score table (8 rows), the heatmap, the history section, and the Skills note from the base files (c4560f2 results.html and benchmark.json) and from HEAD. Four rows carry the provisional flag in both renders. The base page has no Domain trust section.

Step 9 pass at 390 px: the document scroll width 390 equals the viewport width. The matrix box has scroll width 748 px in a client width of 309 px with overflow-x auto. No element sits outside the viewport without a clipping parent. The failure list does not overflow. At 320 px the page does not scroll sideways (box 748 px in 239 px).

Step 10: no page error and no console error from the page code at both widths. At 1280 px the console holds one entry. Chrome asked for /favicon.ico and the static host answered 404. Neither c4560f2 nor HEAD has a favicon file or an icon link in docs/, so this 404 does not come from the phase diff. A stub of that request leaves the console empty.

NFR-6 pass: each cell holds a word. Text contrast on the cell colors is 8.58 (safe), 9.18 (Safe, not optimized), 8.28 (risk), and 6.35 (unproven). All values exceed 4.5. The lede and list text have contrast 6.58 and the sub-line 6.9.
Keyboard pass: the region 'Domain trust matrix' has role region, an aria-label, and tabindex 0. The section stops are the link, then the region. The page has no duplicate id.

Escape test pass: request interception put an img tag with onerror, a b tag, a script tag, and a u tag into the model name, a check id, a kind, a text, and a verdict. The page showed each as literal text. No dialog opened, no element or script appeared, and window.__xss stayed unset. UX-P3-11 covers the six numeric fields.

State checks: the page shows 'Loading results…' first and the section after the data (14 rows). A blocked data request shows 'Could not load benchmark data: Failed to fetch'. UX-P3-10 covers an absent, empty, and malformed domain_trust block.

Stale check: the run ids of the committed export equal the preview for all 14 models. The 16 other stored run directories of those 14 models are invalid or lack score.json or results.json, so none joins the matrix.
Leak scan of the docs/ and README.md diff found no key, token, e-mail address, or home path. Only the check text 'checkout action authorization' matched the word authorization.
Void files: the role did not read, edit, or delete ux-browser-review-6f7451b.json or its log.

Cleanup: the role stopped its own server PID 3655780. The permission layer declined rm for the four temp scripts ux-p3-r2-check1.cjs to ux-p3-r2-check4.cjs. They stay in measure/runs/domain_trust/, which .gitignore line 11 ignores. Delete them.
